fixed.member: Word moves and double presses in text (text fields, areas, user-select text)
fixed.summary: Words come from ICU's segmenter with its dictionaries: Ctrl or Alt with the arrows (Option on a Mac), word deletes and a double press stop at the words of Thai, Lao, Khmer, Myanmar, Chinese and Japanese, which are written without spaces, where they stepped a cluster or a character at a time.

The caret, the selection and what Backspace and Delete remove come from Parley's editor over the text as it is laid out: ← and → step a grapheme cluster on screen, through a right-to-left run from the side they enter it; ↑ and ↓ keep the caret's column; a press lands on the cluster drawn under it in every face. Backspace removes one character of a cluster (an accent, a Thai tone mark, an Indic vowel sign) as platform text fields do, and a whole emoji or line break; Delete removes the cluster after the caret.

Moves frames: its lines break as labels do (UAX #14), so Thai breaks between words and Chinese and Japanese between characters, where an area broke only at spaces (or mid-word when a word was wider than the line).
